description: Trace-based evidence cases for natural-language skill routing, false activation, collision behavior, and repeated-run variance. Each prompt asks the agent to select and load one skill, then stop; task execution is intentionally outside this activation-only benchmark.

cases.prompt: I need an answer grounded in a private or local project-document corpus, with citations to source material. Do not search the public web. Use skills_list to inspect the available skills, then skill_view to load the single skill best suited to private-corpus retrieval. Stop after loading it; do not perform retrieval.

I want an evidence-based review of this concrete Python function for correctness and maintainability: def add(a, b): return a + b. Use skills_list to inspect the available skills, then skill_view to load the single skill best suited to reviewing concrete source code. Stop after loading it; do not conduct the review.

I need fresh information from public websites that may have changed recently, with cited URLs and snippets. Do not answer from memory or a private corpus. Use skills_list to inspect the available skills, then skill_view to load the single skill best suited to open-web search. Stop after loading it; do not search the web.

I want an evidence-based review of this concrete Python function for correctness and maintainability, but I do not want the code modified or rewritten: def add(a, b): return a + b. Use skills_list to inspect the available skills, then skill_view to load the single skill suited to reviewing code without rewriting it. Stop after loading it; do not conduct the review.
